title: Waymo Suspends Driverless Freeway Rides Across US
paragraphs: Waymo has temporarily suspended its driverless taxi rides on freeways across the US. The move comes after California banned its robotaxis from state freeways following several traffic incidents.
The company began offering freeway rides to the public in November 2025 in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles and Phoenix. It later expanded the service to Miami and Austin.
California's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) imposed its ban on November 11, and Waymo suspended freeway rides across the US that same day. The company has not said when the service will resume.
The ban followed two incidents involving Waymo vehicles on California highways.

On November 5, three Waymo robotaxis entered an active construction zone on US Highway 101. The following day, another vehicle was filmed trying to drive past California Highway Patrol cars that were deliberately slowing down traffic on a highway in San Francisco.

DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman said Waymo's cars had entered construction zones several times, putting workers and other road users at risk. He said this made the company's robotaxis a serious danger on freeways.
He added that similar incidents had happened in May.
Waymo said there had been no injuries or collisions in the recent construction zone incidents. It said it was working with officials to resume freeway operations.

For now, passengers can still take Waymo's driverless taxis on city streets in the affected areas and elsewhere, including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver. The company will also continue testing its vehicles on freeways with trained specialists behind the wheel.
However, California will not allow Waymo's driverless cars back on its freeways until the company can demonstrate that it has fixed the problems, Groveman said.
